Regional headquarters of of Worldwide Veterinary Service (Thailand). Their mission is to improve animal welfare in Southeast Asia through veterinary treatment and rehabilitation for stray and community animals as well as free sterilization and vaccination campaigns, to break the cycle of suffering caused by the massive stray overpopulation.

Also a great place to find a new furry family member. There are many fully recovered and well socialized dogs available for adoption!

It’s a great place to visit, meet some of the rescued animals and learn about sustainable animal welfare work.

Hello, I'd like to share my review of WVS. There are many stray dogs in my neighborhood, and because they're mostly free-roaming, the number of stray puppies is constantly increasing. I'm one of the people who feeds and waters them. Recently, one of my dogs was hit by a car. Someone took him to the side of the road, but he kept trying to crawl back to my house where I usually feed him. However, I noticed something was wrong; he wasn't as cheerful as usual and wouldn't come begging for food. I asked the elderly woman who usually hangs him at a restaurant, and learned that he'd been hit by a car and couldn't stand. The driver didn't even stop to check on him. He was in pain, couldn't defecate, and his stomach was very swollen. I took him to the hospital, but they only did X-rays and blood tests, which were quite expensive. The vet said further treatment would start at 60,000 baht, but they couldn't guarantee it. So I consulted with WVS. They read my message and called immediately, recommending that I bring my dog ​​to them for treatment. The treatment took almost a month, and now he's completely recovered. There were no treatment costs at all. I want to express my deepest gratitude for helping these stray dogs regain their happiness.

I think many people don't know that Chiang Mai has a free dog sterilization service. Thank you so much to WVS! I recently took my dog ​​there for sterilization, and he had to stay overnight for recovery because they said it might be finished in the evening. They also have dogs looking for homes here. I regret not knowing about this place sooner. If you're hesitant, I highly recommend it!

text: WVS is a wonderful place. It's clean and safe. My mother called the staff to help pick up our dog, who was seriously ill, with a rope around her neck causing a foul odor and almost severing her throat. WVS staff took the dog in for treatment until she recovered completely and returned her to my mother. Her name is Thua Ngok (meaning "sprout"), and she is now very healthy. Another dog, Zebra, had uterine cancer, and WVS staff took her in for treatment. Zebra has also recovered and is under my mother's care. On August 15th, 2023, my mother had the dogs spayed and took them home. All three dogs—Thua Ngok, Zebra, and Bear—are now under my mother's care. We would like to express our deepest gratitude to the WVS staff. May you all have continued happiness and prosperity. 🙏
